versionChangelog.title: VigiSensys {version}
versionChangelog.description: Version 1.1: redesigned alarm acknowledgement, secured SMTP configuration and clearer location validation.

items.0: From Monitoring, the acknowledgement action now opens the alarm and location analysis directly.
items.1: Location alarms remain visible on the left, can be selected together and stay greyed as “Acknowledged” until the page is refreshed.
items.2: Analysis now focuses only on the actual alarm period, without a date-range selector or Audit tab.
items.3: Analysis export is now a single XLSX with Presentation, measurements and the embedded chart when available.

items.0: Adjustment and calibration workflows are more reliable with plateau acquisitions, A/B/C coefficients, explicit hardware errors and rollback after partial failures.
items.1: Calibration PDF reports and ZIP exports can now export one operation or several historical operations at once.
items.2: SEF standards are supported directly through Sollae TCP converters without an ezVSP virtual COM port.
items.3: GSP/GSO coefficients are read, displayed and synchronized without automatically overwriting the configuration already stored in probes.
items.4: Adjustment import supports unassigned probes, multi-module assignment and keeps database import separate from hardware synchronization.

items.0: Administration > Settings is organised into General, Security, Alarms & notifications, and Services tabs.
items.1: Any SMTP change must now be confirmed with a 6-digit code sent through the new configuration before business emails resume.
items.2: Mailing activation is available directly on its card and its validation state is visible from the Admin Dashboard.
items.3: Creating or editing a location displays the selected probe range and blocks out-of-range setpoints, thresholds or pre-alarms before submission.
items.4: Location APIs also return the precise out-of-range reason instead of a generic validation message.

items.0: First login now has a dedicated onboarding flow and follows the configured password policy.
items.1: The Better Auth foundation is integrated as an opt-in feature with controlled activation and compatibility with the legacy flow.
items.2: Password reset no longer reports a successful delivery when SMTP failed and avoids revealing whether an account exists.
items.3: Email links are localized and the Legal notice / Data protection pages document the standard on-premise VigiSensys model.

items.0: Twilio is ready as the recommended test-call provider, including Trial account support and a deployment guide.
items.1: OVHcloud Click2Call and Asterisk/SIP remain documented options depending on the customer's infrastructure.
items.2: Telephony features are protected by the corresponding license option in both APIs and the user interface.

items.0: The Web component moves to version 1.1.0; Server, Agent and database revisions remain independently versioned.
items.1: The new acknowledgement flow preserves existing permission checks and invalidates application caches after processing.
items.2: Alarm chart loading covers the complete relevant period, including alarms fully contained within the current day.
items.3: This update requires no database schema migration and remains compatible with MySQL and SQL Server.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before moving to Standard.

0.question: Does data leave our site ?
0.answer: No. VigiSensys runs 100% on-premise. No data goes through the cloud. Everything stays on your local infrastructure.

1.question: Does it work without internet ?
1.answer: Yes. The system runs on a full LAN. Internet is not required for daily operations.

2.question: How does the upgrade work ?
2.answer: Simple: a new license key and a service restart if needed. You can move from Pack to One, Standard, or Expert without data loss.

3.question: What MC2 support is available ?
3.answer: Technical support, on-site interventions, training. Options tailored to your needs.

4.question: What is the update policy ?
4.answer: Updates are included with the active license. Deployment is controlled by your IT teams, at your pace.

performance.title: Performance tests
performance.description: Test pages to measure the impact of Next.js 16 cache on each section. Compare timings before/after optimization (~20-50ms vs ~1000-2000ms).

guide.title: How to use performance tests ?
guide.step1_description: Open DevTools > Network, clear cache (Ctrl+Shift+Del), reload. Note the timing (~1000-2000ms without cache).
guide.step2_description: Reload several times (F5). Next.js 16 cache serves data instantly (~20-50ms). Improvement of 50x to 100x.
guide.step3_description: In each page folder, rename `page.tsx` and `page-old.tsx` to test the client-only version (without optimization).
guide.build_description: Measure real production timings (~5-15ms with cache).
